Board of Commissioners, was indicted on one count of Aiding and Assisting
the Preparation of a False Tax Return, one count of Wire Fraud Conspiracy,

Section 45-5-6(b) and received on August 19, 2026; and

by Code Section 45-5-6(e) has passed.

AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS

HEREBY

affected thereby and to make a written report to me within 14 days of this
Order with a recommendation as to whether Mr. Banes should be

Department, died in the line of duty on September 2, 2026; and

a law enforcement officer and was a great representative of the public safety
community; and

Prior to his service with the Warm Springs Police Department, Sgt. Fisher worked
for the Meriwether County Sheriffs Office, Fayette County Sheriffs Office, and
Heard County Sheriffs Office; and

Sgt. Fisher also proudly served his country for five years in the United States Army
as a Transportation Specialist; and

It is fitting and proper to recognize Sgt. Fisher’s service to his fellow Georgians by
lowering the flags on the State Capitol building and in Meriwether, Fayette, and
Heard Counties to half-staff.

NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR OF AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE

Code Section 20-2-73 provides that when a local school system or school
has been placed on the level of accreditation immediately preceding loss of
accreditation, the State Board of Education shall conduct a hearing to
determine whether to recommend the suspension of members of a local
board of education; and

The State Board of Education, following such a hearing, recommended to
me the suspension of all eligible members of the Dublin City Board of
Education; and

On August 17, 2026, I issued Executive Order 08.17.26.01, suspending all
eligible members of the Dublin City Board of Education and creating the
Dublin City Board of Education Nominating Committee, pursuant to Code
Section 20-2-73; and

The Dublin City Board of Education Nominating Committee sent its
nominations to me for temporary replacements to appoint to the Dublin
City Board of Education on August 31, 2026; and

Code Section 20-2-73 provides that, upon suspension, the Governor shall
“appoint temporary replacement members who shall otherwise be qualified
to serve” as members of the local board of education; and

Such temporary replacement members shall become permanent members
of the local board of education upon the conclusion of the appeal process set
forth in Code Section 20-2-73(b) and (c).

BY THE GOVERNOR:


                            FLAGS ON ALL STATE BUILDINGS AND GROUNDS
                                ORDERED LOWERED TO HALF STAFF


   WHEREAS: Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean was an exceptional talent, singer, songwriter, actress,
            philanthropist, businesswoman, and American treasure, as well as a woman of
            joyful and enduring faith; and

   WHEREAS: Born in a one-room cabin in Tennessee in the Smoky Mountains, Dolly was the
            fourth of twelve children and grew up in a family she called “dirt poor,” but one
            rich in faith and joy – an upbringing she memorialized in songs like “My Tennessee
            Mountain Home,” and “Coat of Many Colors;” and

   WHEREAS: Dolly moved to Nashville the day after graduating high school to begin what would
            ultimately be an historic country music career, meeting the man who would
            become her husband of nearly 59 years, Carl Thomas Dean, the very same day. Two
            years later in 1966, they married in Ringgold, Georgia, in part because the town’s
            name reminded her of "rings of gold," which she took as a good sign for her
            marriage; and

   WHEREAS: Spanning over seven decades, Dolly’s extraordinary career earned her 25 No. 1
            country singles; 11 Grammy Awards; induction into both the Country Music Hall
            of Fame and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame; many arts and humanities honors;
            starring roles in movies like “9 to 5,” “Steel Magnolias,” Joyful Noise,” and others;
            numerous television appearances; and fame around the world; and

   WHEREAS: Of all her many achievements and honors, perhaps the most long-lasting and
            meaningful is Dolly Parton's abiding place in the hearts and memories of so many
            who appreciated her genuine kindness, her larger-than-life talents, and her
            sincerity when she sang those timeless lyrics: “I will always love you;” and

   WHEREAS: It is fitting and proper to honor Dolly Parton’s memory by lowering the flags on all
            State buildings and grounds to half-staff.
           NOW, THEREFORE, IN HONOR AND AS A MARK OF RESPECT FOR THE MEMORY OF
           DOLLY PARTON, PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF
           THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

ORDERED:   That the flag of the United States and the flag of the State of Georgia be flown at
           half-staff on all state buildings and grounds for a one-week period beginning at
           sunrise on Wednesday, August 26, 2026.

           This 25th day of August 2026.

five counts of Hobbs Act Extortion Under Color of Official Right and one count of

Acertified copy of the indictment was transmitted to me pursuant to Code Section
45-5-6(b) and received on July 16, 2026; and

On July 31, 2026, I appointed members to the review commission to determine
whether the indictment relates to and adversely affects the administration of the
Office of Sheriff of Burke County such that the rights and interests of the public are
adversely affected thereby and to make a written report to me within 14 days with
a recommendation as to whether Mr. Williams should be suspended from office;
and

By report dated August 10, 2026, the review commission found that the indictment
relates to and adversely affects the administration of the Office of Sheriff of Burke
County such that the rights and interests of the public are adversely affected
thereby and recommended that Mr. Williams be suspended from office in
accordance with Code Section 45-5-6.

NOW, THEREFORE, PURSUANT TO CODE SECTION 45-5-6, AND THE AUTHORITY
VESTED IN ME AS GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF GEORGIA, IT IS HEREBY

That Mr. Williams is hereby suspended from the Office of Sheriff of Burke County
immediately and without further action pending the final disposition of the case or
until the expiration of his term of office, whichever occurs first, as provided by
Code Section 45-5-6(c).

                        GEORGIA WILDFIRE RECOVERY


 WHEREAS:    On April 22, 2026, I issued Executive Order No. 04.22.26.01, declaring a
             State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires in 91 counties in South Georgia
             that were at high risk for wildfires; and

 WHEREAS:    The State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires adopted and incorporated an
             administrative order from the Georgia Forestry Commission implementing
             a temporary burn ban in the counties covered by the declaration; and

 WHEREAS:    On May 5, 2026, I issued Executive Order No. 05.05.26.01, which lifted the
             State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires in all counties except for Appling,
             Atkinson, Bacon, Berrien, Brantley, Camden, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee,
             Echols, Glynn, Jeff Davis, Lanier, Lowndes, Pierce, Ware, and Wayne
             counties; and

 WHEREAS:    On May 12, 2026, I issued Executive Order No. 05.12.26.01, which lifted the
             temporary burn ban in all counties, among other provisions; and

 WHEREAS:    The State of Emergency for Georgia Wildfires expired Friday, May 22, 2026,
             at 11:59 P.M.; and

 WHEREAS:    Additional assistance from the State is necessary to support recovery efforts
             after these unprecedented wildfires and harvest the remaining salvageable
             timber while it is still economically feasible; and

 WHEREAS:    The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as the Chief
             Executive of this State; and

 WHEREAS:    As Chief Executive, the Governor is tasked with declaring a state of

STATE OF EMERGENCY FOR
ACUTE CONSUMER PRICE SHOCK

- Global markets remain unstable and are subjecting Georgians to

unpredictable price shocks on basic goods and services; and

The factors driving these market shifts are inherently unpredictable,
and therefore, difficult, if not impossible, for the citizens of our State
to budget for, exacerbating the impact on hardworking Georgians;
and

Brent crude futures, a global benchmark for oil prices, rose more
than three percent on Friday, May 15, 2026, alone, and other index
prices have similarly fluctuated dramatically over the past weeks;
and

It is necessary to take proactive measures to insulate Georgia’s
citizens from these acute price fluctuations, so that families and
small businesses can budget appropriately and better ensure their
long-term financial stability; and

The upcoming Memorial Day holiday is already a period of elevated
travel and corresponding upward pressure on gas prices from the
increased demand; and

The General Assembly passed a temporary, 60-day suspension of
motor fuel taxes on March 20, 2026, and such suspension is set to
expire at the end of the day on May 19, 2026, further amplifying the
harmful consumer effects mentioned above; and

Code Section 45-12-22 vests the Governor with the power to suspend
the collection of state motor fuel taxes during a declared state of
emergency, subject to the ratification by the General Assembly at its
next meeting; and

The Governor is vested with the emergency powers cited herein as
the Chief Executive of this State; and

Severe drought conditions existing across southeastern Georgia have
created an extreme and widespread threat for wildfires; and

The National Weather Service reports an elevated fire danger across
southeastern Georgia as gusty winds and low humidity continue to
exacerbate persistent drought conditions; and

Since April 18, 2026, the Georgia Forestry Commission has
responded to over 90 wildfires in the State; and

As of April 22, 2026, the Pineland Road Fire in Clinch and Echols

10 percent contained, and the Highway 82 Wildfire in Brantley
County has burned over 5,000 acres and is only 10 percent
contained; and

These unprecedented fire occurrences have spread and intensified
rapidly due to the woody debris remaining in South Georgia from
Hurricane Helene; and

In response to the multiple active wildfires, many local governments
have issued evacuation orders and local burning bans; and

Due to the hazardous wildfire conditions throughout the State, on
April 22, 2026, the Georgia Forestry Commission issued a 30-day
ban on outdoor burning across 91 counties; and

On April 21 and 22, 2026, the Federal Emergency Management
Agency approved Georgia’s request for a Fire Management
Assistance Grant for the Pineland Road Wildfire and the Highway 82
Wildfire, respectively; and

The National Weather Service issued a Winter Storm Watch for
North Georgia beginning late Friday, January 23, 2026, through

social and economic welfare of the State; and
